title: Installing a Skill in the Project
description: A shell heredoc that creates .agents/skills/commit-message and writes its SKILL.md. A skill is just a directory holding a SKILL.md, so installing one is putting a folder where opencode looks.

steps.description: This installs the `commit-message` skill into the project path. A skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md`, and that is the entire mechanism: opencode walks the filesystem, reads each `SKILL.md`, and offers the skill to the model.
`mkdir -p .agents/skills/commit-message` makes the skill directory. The page recommends `.agents/skills/`, which both opencode and pi read, so your skills are not welded to one tool.
`cat > .agents/skills/commit-message/SKILL.md <<'MD'` writes the file from the heredoc that follows. The quoted delimiter keeps the contents literal.

The front matter between the `---` fences holds two fields. `name` is `commit-message`, and `description` states when to use the skill: for a commit message, or when the user runs `git commit` without one.

The body is the instruction the model follows. It reads the staged files with `git status --short`, writes a subject line under seventy characters saying what changed and why, adds a blank line and the reasoning if it is not obvious, and does not describe the change line by line.

steps.question: The page says the directory name must match which field, or the skill silently never loads?
